searchText: It's 69 right? yup Hmm we have that sent you a dm now libp2p can't connect due to this: https://docs.rs/libp2p/latest/libp2p/core/upgrade/enum.NegotiationError.html#variant.Failed we suppose you didnt do anything special with libp2p protocol negotiation? <protolambda> The fork digest, computed from configuration and genesis state, is part of the protocol id used in negotiation and exchange of messages. Looking at previous configuration issues, that’s likely the problem here ``` Sep 18 08:40:32.283 DEBG Handshake Failure reason: Incompatible forks Ours:02328408 Theirs:9c671128, peer: 16Uiu2HAmBQRRuf7dZYgoXDcafzdyGzsrA5Gtbet6gyP4r3w7zfkv ``` <protolambda> The forkdigest is a mix of fork version, and genesis validator set hash tree root <protolambda> Probably just need to correct the fork versions in config or change the fork epoch numbers so the node uses the right one > cfg.Eip4844ForkVersion = []byte{0x83, 0x00, 0x0f, 0xfd} it's 83 not 03 ^^ We have 14 minutes left until submission :D getting kinda stressed bc of rust Weird changing that did not change our fork digest Found and fixed it, we're now getting a bunch of "NonLinearParentRoot" errors <dankrad> @xrchz and I are working on extending Ben Edgingtons c-kzg to include high-level functions that will do all the cryptography needed to implement 4844. The implementation work is actually pretty much done (thanks to excellent prior work by Ben), so we now need help to create the right interfaces for clients <dankrad> If you are interested this please join https://t.me/+R677gbCrlVoyYTk0 for discussion <dankrad> Current state of the work is here: https://github.com/dankrad/c-kzg/tree/lagrange_form i was reading Vitalik's DAS/Sharding post (https://hackmd.io/@vbuterin/sharding_proposal#Why-not-just-use-DAS-and-not-committees) and it seems to me that the P2P layer would become extremely complex and potentially easier to disrupt. Is this the plan also for Danksharding? <dankrad> yes. This is definitely one of our biggest concerns right now with full sharding and data availability sampling. we're doing very active research into building robust DAS solutions <protolambda> Thinking about a leaner sampling network solution too, planning to present at devcon :)
